summary.text: Caleb Schwab is the Libertarian candidate for Warrandyte at the 2026 Victorian election. He works as a research assistant and has a biomedical science degree from Deakin University. His party profile says he spent much of his youth in the Warrandyte electorate and argues for smaller, more accountable government.

priorities.text: Government that is accountable all the time, not only at elections
Letting adults make their own decisions and removing needless barriers for people and businesses
Better roads and infrastructure, and relief for struggling small businesses

summary.text: John Stanley is standing for the Victorian Socialists in Warrandyte at the 2026 Victorian election. He describes himself as a student and socialist activist from the area. His campaign calls for much larger public health, housing and education systems paid for by higher taxes on large companies and the very wealthy.

priorities.text: A big expansion of public health, housing and education, funded by taxing corporations and the very rich
Climate action and justice for First Nations people
Defending public housing and opposing new large data centres

summary.text: Nicole Werner is the Liberal MP for Warrandyte, which she won at the 2023 by-election after Ryan Smith retired; she had run unsuccessfully for Box Hill in 2022. A former youth worker and youth pastor, she has held shadow roles since 2025 and is now the opposition spokesperson on home ownership and housing affordability, youth and child protection. She is recontesting Warrandyte in 2026.

summary.text: Rebecca Paterson is Labor's candidate for Warrandyte at the 2026 Victorian election. Labor's page says she grew up in Warrandyte and is a working mother with three daughters. Neither the party nor the ABC had published details of her career as at early November 2026.

priorities.text: Easing cost-of-living pressure on local families
Good local schools and accessible health care
Protecting Warrandyte's bushland, wildlife and green spaces

summary.text: Vanessa Muradian is the Greens candidate for Warrandyte in 2026. The ABC lists her as a sexologist, counsellor and yoga teacher who runs her own business. On the party's site she names climate change, living costs, mental health and the effects of AI among the issues she wants to take on.

occupation.text: Sexologist, counsellor and yoga teacher; business owner

priorities.text: Faster action on the warming climate
Responses to the cost of living, mental health and the rise of AI
Stronger community ties, including with the Birrarung (Yarra) and the surrounding bushland
